# The rendered two-root drag receipt for criterion 10: a tab dragged from one full Workstation root over a second full root never previews, stages or commits there, once two roots can coexist

## Context

#18303's closeout matrix requires, for criterion 10, **L3 — preview and staging absence observed in a second independent full root, with a same-Group positive control**. #18284 (PR #18368) delivers the ownership axis and proves the boundary at two levels: the composed four-participation unit arm (L2) and the cross-window witness — a real browser App Worker driving the real `Neo.manager.DragCoordinator` and real `window/Participation` instances, with injected window rects and a stubbed hit-test (`examples/dashboard/crossWindowWitness/Harness.mjs`, `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockCrossWindowWitnessNL.spec.mjs`). What it cannot deliver is the rendered observation the matrix names: two full Workstation roots on one App SharedWorker, a header tab dragged from root A across root B's window, and root B's own DOM showing no drop indicator, no preview affordance and no staged pane, followed by the same drag committing into root A's own vessel.

The obstacle is #18376: a second full Workstation root kills the first root's renderer (its OffscreenCanvases are driven by the shared App Worker in the first root's process). The topology spec's pane-host second root (`?popout=<pane>`) survives but carries no workspace, so it registers no drag surface a gesture could be foreign to. Until #18376 lands, this receipt cannot be produced in the harness. This ticket owns that residual, so PR #18368's evidence declaration can name it truthfully and #18284 can close on its own acceptance criteria.

## The Problem

Criterion 10 has an owner for its implementation (#18284) but, once #18284 closes, no owner for its L3 receipt. The witness stands in at contract level; the epic's matrix row stays unsatisfied at the level it names.

## The Architectural Reality

- `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs` already boots two roots in one context and reads the manager through root A's live Workspace over the Neural Link; its second root is the pane-host mode for the reason above.
- `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL.spec.mjs` and `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs` drive real cross-window drags from a main window into popups and assert rendered outcomes (`.neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicators:not(.neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicators-hidden)`, `.neo-dock-preview-affordance`, `.neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicator-active`) — the pieces the two-root journey reuses.
- The negative reading must be taken in root B's page while the drag from root A is held over it; the positive control is the same gesture committing into A's own popup, exactly the shape of the witness's journey but rendered.

## The Fix

A `WorkstationTwoRootsDragNL.spec.mjs` journey: boot two full roots (`context.newPage()`), pop a vessel out of each so both hold a popup with the same bare workspace ids under different Groups, drag a header tab from A's main window over B's popup and over B's main window — asserting in B's pages: zero visible drop indicators, zero preview affordances, no staged pane, B's documents byte-identical — then continue the same drag into A's popup and assert exactly one commit there. Runs under `playwright.config.e2e.mjs` once #18376's fix lets two full roots coexist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — The journey exists and is red-first meaningful: with both roots' `resolveOwnershipId` forced to one Group (a measured mutation, not committed), the negative assertions fail; restored, they pass.
- [ ] AC-2 — The negative reading is taken from root B's own DOM during the held drag: no visible drop indicator, no preview affordance, no staged pane; B commits nothing — its commit count and transaction history are unchanged, not only its two documents byte-identical, so a no-op or history-only commit cannot hide behind equal documents.
- [ ] AC-3 — The positive control commits exactly once into root A's own vessel in the same gesture.
- [ ] AC-4 — #18303's criterion-10 row cites this spec as its L3 receipt, and PR #18368's residual is discharged.

## Out of Scope

- Making two full roots coexist — #18376.
- The contract-level witness and the unit arms — delivered by #18284.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-06T09:56:54Z

**This ticket has left #18303's sub-tree. It stays open, and here is exactly why — because the reason is a scope decision, not an abandonment.**

Operator direction, 2026-09-06: one main window with popups is the multi-window story the dock epics own. A user loading the same app in a second **independent** main window is a real scenario and important, but it is being kept **outside** #18303 and #18304, because the thing standing in its way is not a dock defect.

The mechanism, restated so this ticket is self-contained: a second full Workstation root's sparkline `OffscreenCanvas`es are transferred to the App Worker — a SharedWorker hosted in the **first** root's renderer process — and Chromium terminates that process for the cross-process frame sink (`Invalid client ID`, reason 123). A popup is unaffected because it joins its opener's process; an unrelated tab of the same origin does not. Fixing it is a **worker-topology** decision for the worker manager's owner (#18376), possibly its own epic. An epic about dock transactions should not be gated on where workers are hosted.

**What changed here**
- Parent link to #18303 removed. Still blocked by #18376.
- Still open, still mine. The receipt it owns is deferred, not cancelled — merged PR #18368's evidence declaration and @neo-gpt's `[AUTHOR_CONFIRMATION]` on #18303 both cite this number, and those citations should keep resolving to a live ticket.
- The ACs stand as written and need no narrowing: they were always predicated on "once two roots can coexist", which is now explicitly #18376's business.

**One correction I owe the record.** At 09:43Z I put a fork to @neo-gpt — build the journey under a bounded canvas exclusion (root B's `transferControlToOffscreen` throwing through the existing `DomAccess.getOffscreenCanvas` catch), or hold the row — and recommended the first. He accepted it at 09:48Z with careful bounds. **I have retracted that.** It was the wrong question: both options assumed the scenario was in scope, and it is not. Building it would have manufactured a rendered receipt for a configuration a user cannot reach, on the day the epics close. The technique itself remains sound and is recorded here for whoever picks this up after #18376 — root B only, riding the existing catch, with an isolation-breaking red control and a confirmation that dock geometry and item topology survive the exclusion.

**What did not change:** #18284's cross-root isolation implementation is merged and stays. It is cheap and fail-closed, and its contract-level receipts — the cross-window witness on a real App Worker with the real `DragCoordinator` and real `Participation` instances, the composed four-participation unit arm, and the real-product single-root positives — all stand. What defers is only the rendered observation inside a second independent full root.

Against `b0e5fceb919df1add8741da4e53207f3ded0f8e7`, Node 25.9.0, real **headless branded Chrome 156 on macOS** in fresh contexts, serving the owned checkout:

- Both pages loaded `/apps/workstation/index.html` without `?popout`, an opener, a copied topology carrier, or canvas exclusion. Both actual dock Workspaces rendered and remained responsive after the second boot.
- Page-side exact worker IDs agreed: one App SharedWorker. Window IDs, canvas groups and transaction Groups differed. An explicitly addressed Neural Link read confirmed two Workspaces and two live participations, each participation's ownership matching its own Group. Both use bare `workstation-main`, exercising the intended distinct-owner case.
- In a second fresh-context run, the same two-full-root setup used the existing `CanvasGroupPainting` static Sparkline discriminator: both witnesses were adopted (`offscreenRegistered:true`) and visibly drawn; updating A changed A's canvas pixels with B's witness byte-identical, then updating B changed B with A byte-identical. Both roots still answered afterward. This is actual paint observation, not canvas-element counts or changing model values alone.
- Cleanup: both owned browser contexts and loopback server closed; the port refused connections; the original clean resident branch was restored. No shared service or profile changed.
